title: North Carolina civil-rights domain extension
description: Profile-specific structure for a civil-rights-nc contract's `domain` block and for the source verification record that a primary_source_verified attestation must bind. The common contract is enforced independently; this schema adds structure and never loosens it. Runtime rules in scripts/civil_rights_nc.py add the cross-field checks: every validation id is mapped to exactly one rung, machine rungs require a declared command and the primary_source_verified rung forbids one, every primary-source check names the one assertion it verifies, every reference resolves, a claim names exactly one declared defendant and one of that defendant's capacities, governing and adverse authority are distinct legal propositions each targeted by a primary-source check, and SOURCE_VERIFIED / SOURCE_VERIFIED_CLAIM are never authored.

single_line.description: Non-blank and on one physical line: no CR or LF anywhere, stated as a prohibition because an end anchor matches before a trailing newline. The 1991 bound leaves room for the longest key prefix (`citation=` or `operator=`, 9 characters) an attestation line adds, so a schema-valid value can always be attested within the acceptance schema's 2000-character bounded_text limit.

assertion_refs.description: Ids of declared assertions this cell of the matrix rests on. Never empty: an unresolved question is declared as an UNKNOWN assertion, never left blank.

workstream.description: The one linked workstream (Issue #11's twelve tracks) this packet focuses on. It names the packet's focus; it does not limit which tracks a claim's matrix must address.

validation_level.description: One rung of the verification ladder. structural and citation_linked are machine-runnable and must declare a command; primary_source_verified is observed by a non-implementer who actually read the primary source and must not.

fact_status.description: The declarable categories an assertion may carry. A verified status is excluded deliberately: repetition never converts an allegation into a fact, and verification is earned in the acceptance ledger, never authored.

declared_claim_basis.description: What a contract may declare. SOURCE_VERIFIED_CLAIM is never authored; it is derived from an accepted acceptance ledger whose bound records re-verify every assertion the claim rests on.

capacities.description: The capacities this defendant is analyzed in. An entity is analyzed only in entity capacity; a natural person only in individual and/or official capacity.

assertion_ids.description: The assertions establishing this defendant's identity and role. They are part of every claim against this defendant, so a claim cannot be verified while who the defendant is and what they did remains unread.

source_id.description: Where the assertion is made: its provenance, not what verifies it. For an allegation this is the filing that alleges it; for a legal proposition it is the authority the proposition characterizes.

verified_by.description: The contract sources whose primary-source review can verify this assertion. A source verification record covers the assertion only when its source_id is one of these. A legal proposition lists exactly its own source_id; an allegation never lists the filing that alleges it. Empty means the assertion is tracked but nothing declared can verify it.

legal_question.description: The precise legal question this claim poses.

defendant_id.description: Exactly one declared defendant. A claim is never merged across defendants.

capacity.description: Exactly one capacity, which must be one the defendant is analyzed in. A claim is never merged across capacities.

right.description: The specific constitutional right or provision and the theory.

governing_authority.description: Legal propositions stating the elements or requirements, each the target of a primary-source check.

supported_by.description: Assertions tied to evidence for this element; at least one is not a legal proposition.

missing_evidence.description: Declared evidence gaps, each naming one of this claim's elements. Any entry keeps the claim from earning SOURCE_VERIFIED_CLAIM.

assertion_ids.description: At least one is a legal proposition: the defense's legal basis.

threshold_defenses.description: Mandatory: immunity and other threshold defenses vary by defendant, capacity and claim type, so they are analyzed per claim.

assertion_id.description: A legal proposition characterizing what the adverse authority holds; reading that authority verifies the characterization.

adverse_authority.description: Mandatory: the strongest authority against the claim, never the same proposition as the governing authority.

assertion_ids.description: The causation and relief showing for this remedy.

prerequisites.description: Any notice, exhaustion or other prerequisite, or why none applies.

assertion_ids.description: At least one is a legal proposition; an undetermined posture includes an UNKNOWN assertion.
At least one is a legal proposition.
At least one is a legal proposition; an undetermined posture includes an UNKNOWN assertion.

adequate_state_remedy.description: Required when claim_type is NC_CORUM; optional otherwise.

assertion_ids.description: At least one is a legal proposition.

entity_liability.description: The policy-or-custom theory. Required when capacity is entity; optional otherwise.

forum.description: The forum/jurisdiction posture this packet assumes; restated per packet because a worker receives only the packet.

assertions.description: The only unit a source verification record verifies, bound by id through validation_targets, never by text.

claims.description: At most one claim: a bounded packet per claim/defendant/capacity combination.

validation_levels.description: Exactly one ladder rung per contract validation id; no other ids.

validation_targets.description: For every primary_source_verified validation id, and no other, the one declared assertion it verifies. The bound record and the attestation must name the same assertion.

synthetic.description: True when every input is fictional and establishes no real case fact or legal conclusion.

template_child_issue.description: For this template's own dogfood packets only: the child issue the packet reviews.

contract_domain.description: Closed: no undeclared key exists in which an earned status could be written, and SOURCE_VERIFIED / SOURCE_VERIFIED_CLAIM are refused wherever they appear.

revision.description: The work-packet contract revision this observation was made against; checked against the acceptance ledger's binding.

contract_hash.description: The exact contract's hash at that revision; revision numbers are lineage-local, so the hash is checked as well.

dispatch_id.description: The submitted result's dispatch_id when this observation was made; a resubmission under the same contract must be observed again.

artifact_sha256.description: The submitted artifact's identity (its reference and sha256 combined) when this observation was made.

assertion_id.description: The declared assertion this record was consulted to verify; must equal the contract's validation_targets entry for validation_id. A record names its assertion by id, never by text.

source_id.description: The contract source this record reviewed. Record verification refuses a source the contract does not declare, and the record covers its assertion only when this id is in that assertion's verified_by.

source_type.description: A record verifying a legal proposition must be of a primary-law type (constitutional_provision, statute, regulation_or_ordinance, court_rule, case_law, court_order).

citation.description: The precise citation or record identifier of the primary source consulted.

custodian_or_repository.description: Where the original is held; provenance for the source consulted, never the original itself.

observed_content.description: What the primary source actually says, in enough detail to be contradicted. A reference to the preserved original, never a copy of restricted or sensitive content.

outcome.description: A primary source can support, contradict, or be inconclusive on the assertion it was consulted to verify; a contradiction is a material finding, not merely an unmet check.

observed_at.description: When the source was reviewed, RFC 3339; validated as a real calendar value, not only a shape.

operator.description: The person who reviewed the primary source and will record the attestation; never an implementation actor.

artifacts.description: Preserved copies, page images, or excerpts, by reference and digest where integrity matters. Never restricted or sensitive content itself.

source_verification_record.description: The structured record a primary_source_verified attestation binds by digest. It is an operator's declaration the controller cannot authenticate; the digest makes it auditable and immutable once attested.
